edits.before: The cubic has geometric permutation monodromy \(S_3\): it is connected of degree three and its discriminant \(-19683\,t(t-1)/16\) is not a square in \(\overline\mathbb Q(t)\). The subgroup \(H\) for the first branch maps onto its point stabilizer and hence contains an element inducing \((23)\). This sends the support \(\{1,2\}\) to \(\{1,3\}\). Possible Kummer signs do not change the support. The unique Galois-equivariant line is therefore not \(H\)-stable.

edits.before: An explicit obstruction is obtained from \(J=\operatorname{Jac}(y^2=x^5-x-1)\). The polynomial is irreducible modulo 3 and modulo 2 factors as \[(x^2+x+1)(x^3+x^2+1).\] Its Galois group is a transitive degree-five group containing an element of cycle type \((2)(3)\), hence a transposition. A primitive group containing a transposition is \(S_5\). Zarhin’s theorem for this characteristic-zero hyperelliptic Jacobian gives \(\operatorname{End}(J_{\overline\mathbb Q})=\mathbb Z\), and thus \(\operatorname{NS}(J_{\overline\mathbb Q})=\mathbb Z[\Theta]\).

edits.before: Every finite quotient of the completion of the discrete group \(\mathbb Z\) is generated by the rational image of \(1\); its points are therefore rational. The maximal profinite quotient is constant \(\widehat\mathbb Z\), not its cyclotomic twist. A quotient \(\mathbb Z/n\) with nontrivial local cyclotomic action modulo \(n\) distinguishes these group schemes.

edits.before:
Even after correcting the twist, the asserted rational product does not follow. The character sequence \[0\longrightarrow\mu_\infty\longrightarrow
 \overline\mathbb Q_p^\times\longrightarrow
 \overline\mathbb Q_p^\times/\mu_\infty\longrightarrow0\] has no \(G_{\mathbb Q_p}\)-equivariant splitting. The class \([p^{1/n}]\) is Galois-fixed for every \(n>1\), because its conjugates differ by roots of unity. An equivariant section would send it to an element of \(\mathbb Q_p^\times\) with normalized valuation \(1/n\), impossible. An abstract splitting over \(\overline\mathbb Q_p\) need not descend.

This illustrative description is not needed by the subsequent matrix-coefficient proof, which explains the limited severity.

edits.before:
The continuous character \[\widehat\mathbb Z\twoheadrightarrow\mathbb Z_p
 \longrightarrow\mathbb Q_p^\times,\qquad
 t\longmapsto(1+p)^t\] has infinite image; for \(p=2\) use \(5^t\). It is a regular matrix coefficient. Complex conjugation interchanges this function with its inverse. It cannot factor through \(\mathbb G_a\times\widehat\mathbb Z\): a group-like function factoring there is an algebraic character, trivial on \(\mathbb G_a\) and of finite image on the profinite factor. This contradicts the infinite image.
edits.after:
The continuous character \[\widehat{\mathbb Z}\twoheadrightarrow\mathbb Z_p
 \longrightarrow\mathbb Q_p^\times,\qquad
 t\longmapsto(1+p)^t\] has infinite image; for \(p=2\) use \(5^t\). It is a regular matrix coefficient. Complex conjugation interchanges this function with its inverse. It cannot factor through \(\mathbb G_a\times\widehat{\mathbb Z}\): a group-like function factoring there is an algebraic character, trivial on \(\mathbb G_a\) and of finite image on the profinite factor. edits.before:
Location. Lemma 10.1(ii), p. 20. Over \(\mathbb Q\) take \(D=C=\mathbb P^1\), \(f(t)=t^2\), \(x=1\), and a nonzero tangent at \(x\). The map is finite surjective and even unramified at \(x\). Nevertheless \[D\setminus f^{-1}(f(x))=\mathbb P^1\setminus\{-1,1\}\simeq\mathbb G_m,
 \qquad C\setminus\{f(x)\}\simeq\mathbb A^1.\] The asserted map on geometric fundamental groups is \(\widehat\mathbb Z\to1\), which is not injective; the arithmetic map cannot be injective either. Require the restricted map to be finite étale, or delete all branch values and their preimages. The Belyi applications already delete \(\{0,1,\infty\}\), so their finite-index step is unaffected. Existence of a compatible tangent is a local fact and does not establish the claimed global open-subgroup property.
edits.after:

edits.before: The apparent sign discrepancy in Proposition 9.1 is not an error: nonpositive weights on \(\mathcal F(\mathcal L)\) become nonnegative weights on its dual function space. The \(\overline\mathbb Q_p\) coefficient field in Lemma 9.5 and absolute irreducibility in the \(\mathbb Q_p\) clause of Proposition 9.6 were checked on actual images. Text extraction must not erase them. Corollary 9.7 itself is stated with \(\overline\mathbb Q_p\) coefficients. The polarization arguments in P2–P3 were written over \(\mathbb Q_p\) and remain valid after that coefficient extension.
